035/**
036 * Formats a log event using a {@link StringBuilder}. <strong>All formatters should be
037 * thread-safe!</strong>.
038 * <p>
039 * The appender will make sure the {@link StringBuilder} is not shared with multiple
040 * threads so the formatter does not have to synchronize/lock on and should definitely not
041 * do that.
042 * <p>
043 * Because of various invariants the preferred way to compose formatters is to use the
044 * {@linkplain #builder() builder} which will do some optimization like combining static
045 * formatters etc.
046 *
047 * @see #builder()
048 * @see LogFormatter.EventFormatter
049 * @see LogEncoder#of(LogFormatter)
050 * @apiNote This class is sealed. An interface that has the same contract that can be
051 * implemented is {@link EventFormatter}.
052 */
053public sealed interface LogFormatter {
054
055        /**
056         * Formats a log event.
057         * @param output buffer.
058         * @param event log event.
059         * @see EventFormatter
060         */
061        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event);
062
063        /**
064         * See {@link EventFormatter#builder()}.
065         * @return builder.
066         */
067        public static Builder builder() {
068                return new Builder();
069        }
070
071        /**
072         * Create a formatter using event formatter that is a lambda so that
073         * {@code LogFormater.of((o, e) -> ...); } works.
074         * @param e will be returned.
075         * @return passed in formatter.
076         * @apiNote this is for ergonomics because LogFormatter is sealed.
077         */
078        public static EventFormatter of(EventFormatter e) {
079                return e;
080        }
081
082        /**
083         * The line separator formatters end lines and stack trace lines with: <code>\n</code>
084         * on every platform unless {@value LogProperties#GLOBAL_LINE_SEPARATOR_PROPERTY} is
085         * set as a system property.
086         * @return line separator.
087         */
088        public static String lineSeparator() {
089                return Internal.LineSeparator.CURRENT;
090        }
091
092        /**
093         * Ask the formatter if will do anything.
094         * @return true if promises not to write to builder.
095         * @see #noop()
096         */
097        default boolean isNoop() {
098                return NoopFormatter.INSTANCE == this;
099        }
100
101        /**
102         * A special formatter that will do nothing. It is a singleton so identity comparison
103         * can be used.
104         * @return a formatter that implements all formatting interfaces but does nothing.
105         */
106        public static NoopFormatter noop() {
107                return NoopFormatter.INSTANCE;
108        }
109
110        /**
111         * A special formatter that will append static text.
112         *
113         * @param content static text.
114         */
115        public record StaticFormatter(String content) implements LogFormatter {
116                @Override
117                public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
118                        output.append(content);
119                }
120
121                /**
122                 * Creates a new formatter by concat the {@link #content()}. This is mainly used
123                 * by the {@link EventFormatter#builder()} to coalesce multiple static text.
124                 * @param next the text that will follow this formatter.
125                 * @return new formatter.
126                 */
127                public StaticFormatter concat(StaticFormatter next) {
128                        return new StaticFormatter(this.content + next.content);
129                }
130
131                /**
132                 * Coalesce formatters that can be such as {@link StaticFormatter}.
133                 * @param formatters list of formatters in the order of which they will be
134                 * executed.
135                 * @return an array of formatters where static formatters next to each other will
136                 * be coalesced.
137                 */
138                private static LogFormatter[] coalesce(List<? extends LogFormatter> formatters) {
139                        var flattened = CompositeFormatter.flatten(formatters);
140                        List<LogFormatter> resolved = new ArrayList<>();
141                        StaticFormatter current = null;
142                        for (var f : flattened) {
143                                if (f.isNoop()) {
144                                }
145                                else if (current == null && f instanceof StaticFormatter sf) {
146                                        current = sf;
147                                }
148                                else if (current != null && f instanceof StaticFormatter sf) {
149                                        current = current.concat(sf);
150                                }
151                                else if (current != null) {
152                                        resolved.add(current);
153                                        resolved.add(f);
154                                        current = null;
155                                }
156                                else {
157                                        resolved.add(f);
158                                }
159                        }
160                        if (current != null) {
161                                resolved.add(current);
162                        }
163                        return resolved.toArray(new LogFormatter[] {});
164                }
165
166                @Override
167                public String toString() {
168                        return "STATIC['" + content + "']";
169                }
170        }
171
172        /**
173         * Controls how a <code>null</code> key value is written by key values formatters, see
174         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.KeyValuesFormatterBuilder#nullStrategy(KeyValueNullStrategy)}.
175         * The examples below are the default percent encoding; other formats write the same
176         * choices in their own syntax.
177         * <p>
178         * A selected key is treated identically whether it is missing from the
179         * {@link KeyValues} entirely or present but mapped to <code>null</code> -
180         * {@link KeyValues#getValueOrNull(String)} cannot tell those two cases apart, so
181         * neither can this.
182         */
183        @CaseChanging
184        public enum KeyValueNullStrategy {
185
186                /**
187                 * The key is omitted entirely (no key, no <code>=</code>) if its value is
188                 * <code>null</code>.
189                 */
190                SKIP,
191                /**
192                 * A <code>null</code> value is normalized to an empty string, so the key is
193                 * always printed as <code>key=</code> (with nothing after the <code>=</code>)
194                 * regardless of whether the underlying value was <code>null</code> or actually an
195                 * empty string.
196                 */
197                EMPTY,
198                /**
199                 * The <code>null</code>/empty-string distinction is preserved: a
200                 * <code>null</code> value prints just the key with no <code>=</code>, while an
201                 * empty string prints <code>key=</code>. The default; most key values (e.g. MDC)
202                 * are never actually mapped to <code>null</code> in practice, so {@link #SKIP}
203                 * and {@link #KEEP} behave identically until they are.
204                 */
205                KEEP;
206
207        }
208
209        /**
210         * Log formatter builder that is composed of other formatters. The
211         * {@link #add(LogFormatter)} are executed in insertion order. <strong> This builder
212         * is smart and will coalesce and consolidate formatters! </strong> For example if
213         * only formatter is added to the builder it will be returned instead of a new
214         * formatter.
215         */
216        public final static class Builder {
217
218                private List<LogFormatter> formatters = new ArrayList<>();
219
220                private Builder() {
221                }
222
223                /**
224                 * Adds a formatter.
225                 * @param formatter formatter to be added the list of formatters.
226                 * @return this builder.
227                 */
228                public Builder add(LogFormatter formatter) {
229                        formatters.add(formatter);
230                        return this;
231                }
232
233                /**
234                 * Adds an event formatter.
235                 * @param formatter event formatter to be added the list of formatters.
236                 * @return this builder.
237                 */
238                public Builder event(LogFormatter.EventFormatter formatter) {
239                        formatters.add(formatter);
240                        return this;
241                }
242
243                /**
244                 * Append the timestamp in ISO format.
245                 * @return this builder.
246                 */
247                public Builder timeStamp() {
248                        formatters.add(DefaultInstantFormatter.ISO);
249                        return this;
250                }
251
252                /**
253                 * Formatter for {@link LogEvent#timestamp()} derived from standard
254                 * {@link DateTimeFormatter}.
255                 * @param dateTimeFormatter formatter for {@link LogEvent#timestamp()}
256                 * @return this builder.
257                 */
258                public Builder timeStamp(DateTimeFormatter dateTimeFormatter) {
259                        formatters.add(TimestampFormatter.of(dateTimeFormatter));
260                        return this;
261                }
262
263                /**
264                 * Adds the default level formatter.
265                 * @return this builder.
266                 * @see LevelFormatter
267                 */
268                public Builder level() {
269                        formatters.add(LogFormatter.LevelFormatter.of());
270                        return this;
271                }
272
273                /**
274                 * Adds the default logger name formatter.
275                 * @return this builder.
276                 */
277                public Builder loggerName() {
278                        formatters.add(DefaultNameFormatter.LOGGER_NAME_FORMATTER);
279                        return this;
280                }
281
282                /**
283                 * Formats the message by calling
284                 * {@link LogEvent#formattedMessage(StringBuilder)}.
285                 * @return this builder.
286                 */
287                public Builder message() {
288                        formatters.add(DefaultMessageFormatter.MESSAGE_FORMATTER);
289                        return this;
290                }
291
292                /**
293                 * Appends static text.
294                 * @param content static text.
295                 * @return this builder.
296                 * @see StaticFormatter
297                 */
298                public Builder text(String content) {
299                        formatters.add(new StaticFormatter(content));
300                        return this;
301                }
302
303                /**
304                 * Creates a formatter that will print a single key's value, Logback/Log4j2
305                 * <code>%X{key}</code> style: just the raw value (or the fallback, or an empty
306                 * string if neither is present) - no key prefix, no percent encoding. For the
307                 * percent-encoded <code>key=value</code> style instead, see
308                 * {@link #encodedKeyValue(String, String)}.
309                 * @param key key to select.
310                 * @param fallback if the value is null the fallback will be used.
311                 * @return this.
312                 */
313                public Builder keyValue(String key, @Nullable String fallback) {
314                        return add(new LogbackSingleKeyValueFormatter(key, fallback));
315                }
316
317                /**
318                 * Adds all of the event's key values in the default key values format, percent
319                 * encoded like a URI query: <code>requestId=42&amp;user=Ada%20Lovelace</code>. A
320                 * key mapped to <code>null</code> is written alone, without <code>=</code>. This
321                 * is {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.KeyValuesFormatterBuilder} with its
322                 * defaults; use {@link #keyValues(Consumer)} for another format, a selection of
323                 * keys, or other null handling.
324                 * @return this.
325                 */
326                public Builder keyValues() {
327                        return add(new KeyValuesFormatterBuilder().build());
328                }
329
330                /**
331                 * Adds the event's key values as configured on a
332                 * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.KeyValuesFormatterBuilder}, which sets the
333                 * format (percent encoding by default, JSON, JSON5, or logfmt), the keys, and the
334                 * null handling, for example:
335                 * {@snippet :
336                 * LogFormatter.builder()
337                 *      .keyValues(kv -> kv.format(KeyValuesFormatterBuilder.Format.LOGFMT).keys(List.of("requestId", "user")));
338                 * }
339                 * @param consumer configures the key values formatter.
340                 * @return this.
341                 */
342                public Builder keyValues(Consumer<KeyValuesFormatterBuilder> consumer) {
343                        var builder = new KeyValuesFormatterBuilder();
344                        consumer.accept(builder);
345                        return add(builder.build());
346                }
347
348                /**
349                 * Creates a formatter that will print a single key value in percent encoding (RFC
350                 * 3986 URI aka the format usually used in {@link URI#getQuery()}). For Logback/
351                 * Log4j2's <code>%X{key}</code> style instead, see
352                 * {@link #keyValue(String, String)}.
353                 * @param key key to select.
354                 * @param fallback if the value is null the fallback will be used.
355                 * @return this.
356                 */
357                public Builder encodedKeyValue(String key, @Nullable String fallback) {
358                        return add(new SingleKeyValueFormatter(key, fallback));
359                }
360
361                /**
362                 * Appends a space.
363                 * @return this builder.
364                 */
365                public Builder space() {
366                        formatters.add(new StaticFormatter(" "));
367                        return this;
368                }
369
370                /**
371                 * Appends text if throwable is set.
372                 * @param text to append if the throwable is set.
373                 * @return this builder.
374                 */
375                public Builder textIfThrowable(String text) {
376                        formatters.add(of((b, e) -> {
377                                if (e.throwableOrNull() != null) {
378                                        b.append(text);
379                                }
380                        }));
381                        return this;
382                }
383
384                /**
385                 * Appends a newline using {@link LogFormatter#lineSeparator()}.
386                 * @return this builder.
387                 */
388                public Builder newline() {
389                        text(LogFormatter.lineSeparator());
390                        return this;
391                }
392
393                /**
394                 * Appends a thread name : {@link Thread#getName()}.
395                 * @return this builder.
396                 */
397                public Builder threadName() {
398                        formatters.add(DefaultThreadFormatter.THREAD_NAME_FORMATTER);
399                        return this;
400                }
401
402                /**
403                 * Appends a thread ID : {@link Thread#threadId()}.
404                 * @return this builder.
405                 */
406                public Builder threadId() {
407                        formatters.add(DefaultThreadFormatter.THREAD_ID_FORMATTER);
408                        return this;
409                }
410
411                /**
412                 * Appends the events throwable stack trace.
413                 * @return this.
414                 */
415                public Builder throwable() {
416                        formatters.add(ThrowableFormatter.of());
417                        return this;
418                }
419
420                /**
421                 * Appends the events throwable stack trace using a custom
422                 * {@link ThrowableFormatter} (e.g. one created with
423                 * {@link ThrowableFormatter#builder()}).
424                 * @param throwableFormatter formatter to use.
425                 * @return this.
426                 */
427                public Builder throwable(ThrowableFormatter throwableFormatter) {
428                        formatters.add(throwableFormatter);
429                        return this;
430                }
431
432                /**
433                 * Will create a generic log formatter that has the inner formatters coalesced if
434                 * possible and will noop if there are no formatters.
435                 * @return flattened formatter.
436                 */
437                public LogFormatter build() {
438                        var array = StaticFormatter.coalesce(formatters);
439                        if (array.length == 0) {
440                                return NoopFormatter.INSTANCE;
441                        }
442                        if (array.length == 1) {
443                                return array[0];
444                        }
445                        return EventFormatter.of(formatters);
446                }
447
448                /**
449                 * Creates the formatter and starts an encoder builder from it - call
450                 * {@link LogEncoder.Builder#build()} to finish, optionally configuring charset,
451                 * content type, max buffer size, or initial buffer size first.
452                 * @return encoder builder.
453                 * @apiNote for ergonomics
454                 */
455                public LogEncoder.Builder encoder() {
456                        return LogEncoder.builder(build());
457                }
458
459        }
460
461        /**
462         * Generic event formatting that is lambda friendly.
463         */
464        @FunctionalInterface
465        public non-sealed interface EventFormatter extends LogFormatter {
466
467                @Override
468                public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event);
469
470                private static EventFormatter of(List<? extends LogFormatter> formatters) {
471                        return new CompositeFormatter(StaticFormatter.coalesce(formatters));
472                }
473
474        }
475
476        /**
477         * Formats a {@link Level}.
478         */
479        public sealed interface LevelFormatter extends LogFormatter {
480
481                /**
482                 * Formats the level.
483                 * @param output buffer.
484                 * @param level level.
485                 */
486                void formatLevel(StringBuilder output, Level level);
487
488                @Override
489                default void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
490                        formatLevel(output, event.level());
491                }
492
493                /**
494                 * Formats a level.
495                 * @param level level
496                 * @return formatted level as a string.
497                 */
498                default String formatLevel(Level level) {
499                        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
500                        formatLevel(sb, level);
501                        return sb.toString();
502                }
503
504                /**
505                 * Default implementation calls {@link LevelFormatter#toString(Level)}
506                 * @return formatter.
507                 */
508                public static LevelFormatter of() {
509                        return DefaultLevelFormatter.LEVEL_FORMATTER;
510                }
511
512                /**
513                 * Default implementation calls {@link LevelFormatter#rightPadded(Level)}
514                 * @return formatter.
515                 */
516                public static LevelFormatter ofRightPadded() {
517                        return DefaultLevelFormatter.RIGHT_PAD_LEVEL_FORMATTER;
518                }
519
520                /**
521                 * Turns a Level into a SLF4J like level String that is all upper case.
522                 * {@link Level#ALL} is "<code>TRACE</code>", {@link Level#OFF} is
523                 * "<code>ERROR</code>" and {@link Level#WARNING} is "<code>WARN</code>".
524                 * @param level system logger level.
525                 * @return upper case string of level.
526                 */
527                public static String toString(Level level) {
528                        return switch (level) {
529                                case DEBUG -> "DEBUG";
530                                case ALL -> "TRACE";
531                                case ERROR -> "ERROR";
532                                case INFO -> "INFO";
533                                case OFF -> "ERROR";
534                                case TRACE -> "TRACE";
535                                case WARNING -> "WARN";
536                        };
537                }
538
539                /**
540                 * Turns a Level into a SLF4J like level String that is all upper case and same
541                 * length with right padding. {@link Level#ALL} is "<code>TRACE</code>",
542                 * {@link Level#OFF} is "<code>ERROR</code>" and {@link Level#WARNING} is
543                 * "<code>WARN</code>".
544                 * @param level system logger level.
545                 * @return upper case string of level.
546                 */
547                public static String rightPadded(Level level) {
548                        return switch (level) {
549                                case DEBUG -> /*   */ "DEBUG";
550                                case ALL -> /*     */ "TRACE";
551                                case ERROR -> /*   */ "ERROR";
552                                case INFO -> /*    */ "INFO ";
553                                case OFF -> /*     */ "ERROR";
554                                case TRACE -> /*   */ "TRACE";
555                                case WARNING -> /* */ "WARN ";
556                        };
557                }
558
559        }
560
561        /**
562         * Formats event timestamps.
563         */
564        public sealed interface TimestampFormatter extends LogFormatter {
565
566                /**
567                 * The default timestamp format used in many logging frameworks which does not
568                 * have dates and only time at millisecond precision.
569                 * <p>
570                 * It is called TTLL as that is the name of the format where it is used in
571                 * logback, log4j etc.
572                 */
573                public static String TTLL_TIME_FORMAT = "HH:mm:ss.SSS";
574
575                /**
576                 * Format timestamp.
577                 * @param output buffer.
578                 * @param instant timestamp.
579                 */
580                void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant);
581
582                @Override
583                default void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
584                        formatTimestamp(output, event.timestamp());
585                }
586
587                /**
588                 * Formats timestamp using {@link #TTLL_TIME_FORMAT}.
589                 * @return formatter.
590                 */
591                public static TimestampFormatter of() {
592                        return DefaultInstantFormatter.TTLL;
593                }
594
595                /**
596                 * Formats a timestamp using ISO format at fixed millisecond precision (e.g.
597                 * {@code 2023-11-14T22:13:20.123Z}, always exactly 3 fractional digits). Pair
598                 * with {@link #ofMicros()} to append additional sub-millisecond digits, similar
599                 * to Logback's {@code %d{ISO8601}%microsecond}.
600                 * @return formatter.
601                 */
602                public static TimestampFormatter ofISO() {
603                        return DefaultInstantFormatter.ISO;
604                }
605
606                /**
607                 * Micro seconds over the events last second. This is for logback compatibility.
608                 * @return microseconds zero padded.
609                 */
610                public static TimestampFormatter ofMicros() {
611                        return MicrosInstantFormatter.INSTANCE;
612                }
613
614                /**
615                 * Formats a timestamp using standard JDK date time formatter.
616                 * @param dateTimeFormatter date time formatter.
617                 * @return timestamp formatter.
618                 */
619                public static TimestampFormatter of(DateTimeFormatter dateTimeFormatter) {
620                        return of(dateTimeFormatter, false);
621                }
622
623                /**
624                 * Formats a timestamp using standard JDK date time formatter.
625                 * <p>
626                 * Formatting with {@link DateTimeFormatter} is comparatively expensive to do on
627                 * every event, so if the caller knows the formatter's finest resolution is
628                 * milliseconds (e.g. a pattern using at most {@code SSS}, never
629                 * {@code n}/{@code N} nanosecond fields), {@code cacheMillisecondPrecision} can
630                 * be set to {@code true} to reuse the previously formatted string whenever
631                 * consecutive events land in the same millisecond - the same trick Logback's
632                 * {@code CachingDateFormatter} and Log4j2's {@code FixedDateFormat} use. Passing
633                 * {@code true} for a formatter that can actually render sub-millisecond precision
634                 * will silently truncate that precision, so only pass {@code true} when the
635                 * pattern is known to not exceed millisecond resolution.
636                 * @param dateTimeFormatter date time formatter.
637                 * @param cacheMillisecondPrecision {@code true} if the formatter's output is
638                 * fully determined by the instant's millisecond value.
639                 * @return timestamp formatter.
640                 */
641                public static TimestampFormatter of(DateTimeFormatter dateTimeFormatter, boolean cacheMillisecondPrecision) {
642                        return new DateTimeFormatterInstantFormatter(dateTimeFormatter, cacheMillisecondPrecision);
643                }
644
645        }
646
647        /**
648         * Formats a throwable.
649         */
650        public non-sealed interface ThrowableFormatter extends LogFormatter {
651
652                /**
653                 * Formats a throwable and appends.
654                 * @param output buffer.
655                 * @param throwable throwable.
656                 */
657                void formatThrowable(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable);
658
659                @Override
660                default void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
661                        var t = event.throwableOrNull();
662                        if (t != null) {
663                                formatThrowable(output, t);
664                        }
665                }
666
667                /**
668                 * Default implementation uses {@link Throwable#printStackTrace(PrintWriter)}.
669                 * This formatter is equivalent to {@code of(Integer.MAX_VALUE, List.of())} except
670                 * that it defers entirely to {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()} and thus will
671                 * respect any override of that method a particular {@link Throwable} subclass
672                 * might have.
673                 * @return formatter.
674                 */
675                public static ThrowableFormatter of() {
676                        return DefaultThrowableFormatter.INSTANT;
677                }
678
679                /**
680                 * Creates a builder for a throwable formatter that can limit the number of stack
681                 * frame lines shown for each throwable in the cause/suppressed chain, exclude
682                 * frames matching regular expressions, and append packaging data. The output is
683                 * otherwise formatted like {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()}: common frames
684                 * shared with the enclosing throwable are elided the same way (e.g.
685                 * <code>"... 6 more"</code>) as long as the depth limit was not what stopped
686                 * printing; if the depth limit is what stopped printing a
687                 * <code>"... N frames truncated"</code> line is emitted instead.
688                 * @return builder.
689                 * @apiNote a builder left at its defaults (no max lines, exclusions, or packaging
690                 * data) builds {@link #of()} itself; otherwise the built formatter walks
691                 * {@link Throwable#getCause()}/{@link Throwable#getSuppressed()}/
692                 * {@link Throwable#getStackTrace()} directly instead of calling
693                 * {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()} and thus will not honor a custom override
694                 * of that method.
695                 */
696                public static Builder builder() {
697                        return new Builder();
698                }
699
700                /**
701                 * Convenience to append a throwable to string builder.
702                 * @param b buffer.
703                 * @param t throwable.
704                 * @apiNote this call creates garbage.
705                 */
706                public static void appendThrowable(StringBuilder b, Throwable t) {
707                        /*
708                         * TODO optimize
709                         */
710                        t.printStackTrace(Internal.StringBuilderPrintWriter.of(b));
711                }
712
713                /**
714                 * Builds a configurable {@link ThrowableFormatter}.
715                 *
716                 * @see ThrowableFormatter#builder()
717                 */
718                public final class Builder {
719
720                        private int maxLines = Integer.MAX_VALUE;
721
722                        private List<String> excludes = List.of();
723
724                        private boolean packagingData = false;
725
726                        private boolean rootCauseFirst = false;
727
728                        private Builder() {
729                        }
730
731                        /**
732                         * Maximum number of stack frame ("at ...") lines printed per throwable in the
733                         * chain. Use {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} for no limit (the default, and matches
734                         * {@link ThrowableFormatter#of()} for well behaved throwables). {@code 0}
735                         * prints just the throwable header lines (class and message) for the whole
736                         * chain with no frames at all.
737                         * @param maxLines maximum stack frame lines per throwable.
738                         * @return this builder.
739                         */
740                        public Builder maxLines(int maxLines) {
741                                this.maxLines = maxLines;
742                                return this;
743                        }
744
745                        /**
746                         * Regular expressions matched with {@link Matcher#find()} against each
747                         * frame's {@link StackTraceElement#toString()}. A frame matching any of these
748                         * is omitted entirely and does not count against {@link #maxLines(int)}.
749                         * Defaults to empty (no filtering).
750                         * @param excludes exclude patterns.
751                         * @return this builder.
752                         */
753                        public Builder excludes(List<String> excludes) {
754                                this.excludes = excludes;
755                                return this;
756                        }
757
758                        /**
759                         * Whether to append packaging data (the jar or module a frame's class was
760                         * loaded from, and its version) after each frame line, e.g.
761                         * <code>[myapp-1.0.jar:1.0]</code> or <code>[java.base:na]</code>. This
762                         * mirrors (but does not byte-for-byte match) logback's
763                         * <code>ExtendedThrowableProxyConverter</code> output. Resolution requires
764                         * loading the frame's class (without initializing it) and can fail silently
765                         * to <code>[na:na]</code> for frames whose class cannot be loaded (e.g.
766                         * dynamically generated classes). This has a real per-frame cost so it
767                         * defaults to <code>false</code>.
768                         * @param packagingData true to append packaging data.
769                         * @return this builder.
770                         */
771                        public Builder packagingData(boolean packagingData) {
772                                this.packagingData = packagingData;
773                                return this;
774                        }
775
776                        /**
777                         * Whether to print the root cause first instead of last, working back up
778                         * through each wrapping exception ("Wrapped by: ..." instead of "Caused by:
779                         * ..."), mirroring logback's
780                         * <code>RootCauseFirstThrowableProxyConverter</code> (<code>%rEx</code>/
781                         * <code>%rootException</code>). Frame trimming (common-frame elision against
782                         * each throwable's own wrapper, {@link #maxLines(int)},
783                         * {@link #excludes(List)}) behaves identically either way - only the print
784                         * order and the "Caused by:"/"Wrapped by:" captions differ. Defaults to
785                         * <code>false</code>.
786                         * @param rootCauseFirst true to print the root cause first.
787                         * @return this builder.
788                         */
789                        public Builder rootCauseFirst(boolean rootCauseFirst) {
790                                this.rootCauseFirst = rootCauseFirst;
791                                return this;
792                        }
793
794                        /**
795                         * Builds the formatter. If none of {@link #maxLines(int)},
796                         * {@link #excludes(List)}, {@link #packagingData(boolean)}, or
797                         * {@link #rootCauseFirst(boolean)} were set away from their defaults, returns
798                         * {@link ThrowableFormatter#of()} (i.e. plain
799                         * {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()} behavior) instead of constructing a
800                         * formatter that walks the throwable manually for no reason.
801                         * @return formatter.
802                         */
803                        public ThrowableFormatter build() {
804                                if (maxLines == Integer.MAX_VALUE && excludes.isEmpty() && !packagingData && !rootCauseFirst) {
805                                        return ThrowableFormatter.of();
806                                }
807                                List<Pattern> compiled = excludes.isEmpty() ? List.of()
808                                                : excludes.stream().map(Pattern::compile).toList();
809                                var resolver = packagingData ? new PackagingDataResolver() : null;
810                                var framePrinter = new ThrowableFramePrinter(maxLines, compiled, resolver);
811                                if (rootCauseFirst) {
812                                        return new RootCauseFirstThrowableFormatter(framePrinter);
813                                }
814                                return new StandardThrowableFormatter(framePrinter);
815                        }
816
817                }
818
819        }
820
821        /**
822         * Tests if the log formatter is noop or is null which will be considered as noop.
823         * @param logFormatter formatter which <strong>can be <code>null</code></strong>!
824         * @return true if the formatter should not be used.
825         */
826        public static boolean isNoopOrNull(@Nullable LogFormatter logFormatter) {
827                return logFormatter == null || logFormatter.isNoop();
828        }
829
830        /**
831         * Pads the right hand side of text with space.
832         * @param sb buffer.
833         * @param s string that will be appended first (left hand) and will not be longer than
834         * the <code>n</code> parameter.
835         * @param n the size of string. If the size is bigger than passed in string the result
836         * will have padding otherwise the passed in string will be cut to the size of this
837         * parameter.
838         */
839        public static void padRight(StringBuilder sb, CharSequence s, int n) {
840                int length = s.length();
841                if (length >= n) {
842                        sb.append(s, 0, n);
843                        return;
844                }
845                sb.append(s);
846                spacePad(sb, n - length);
847        }
848
849        /**
850         * Pads the left hand side of text with space.
851         * @param sb buffer.
852         * @param s string that will be appended second (right hand) and will not be longer
853         * than the <code>n</code> parameter.
854         * @param n the size of string. If the size is bigger than passed in string the result
855         * will have padding otherwise the passed in string will be cut to the size of this
856         * parameter.
857         */
858        public static void padLeft(StringBuilder sb, CharSequence s, int n) {
859                int length = s.length();
860                if (length >= n) {
861                        sb.append(s, 0, n);
862                        return;
863                }
864                spacePad(sb, n - length);
865                sb.append(s);
866        }
867
868        /**
869         * Fast space padding method.
870         */
871        private static void spacePad(final StringBuilder sbuf, final int length) {
872                int l = length;
873                while (l >= 32) {
874                        sbuf.append(CompositeFormatter.SPACES[5]);
875                        l -= 32;
876                }
877
878                for (int i = 4; i >= 0; i--) {
879                        if ((l & (1 << i)) != 0) {
880                                sbuf.append(CompositeFormatter.SPACES[i]);
881                        }
882                }
883        }
884
885        /**
886         * A special formatter that will do nothing.
887         */
888        enum NoopFormatter implements TimestampFormatter, ThrowableFormatter, LevelFormatter {
889
890                /**
891                 * instance.
892                 */
893                INSTANCE;
894
895                @Override
896                public void formatThrowable(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable) {
897                }
898
899                @Override
900                public void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant) {
901                }
902
903                @Override
904                public void formatLevel(StringBuilder output, Level level) {
905                }
906
907                @Override
908                public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
909                }
910
911        }
912
913        /**
914         * Rewrites the text a formatter has just written for an event, for example to prefix
915         * every line or to escape line breaks. Unlike a formatter, a post processor sees the
916         * finished text of the whole event, including message arguments and stack traces.
917         * <p>
918         * Post processors apply only to encoders backed by a formatter, such as the default
919         * encoder, the pattern encoder and {@link LogEncoder#of(LogFormatter)}. Encoders that
920         * write bytes directly, such as the JSON encoders, ignore them. They are selected by
921         * name with the {@value LogEncoder#ENCODER_POST_PROCESSORS_PROPERTY} property: <pre>
922         * logging.appender.console.encoder.postProcessors=crlf,journald
923         * </pre>
924         * <p>
925         * They run in the order listed, each on the text the previous one left, so the order
926         * changes the result. With <code>crlf,journald</code> a multi-line event becomes one
927         * line with one prefix. With <code>journald,crlf</code> every original line is
928         * prefixed and then the lines are joined.
929         * <p>
930         * A post processor changes only the text of the encoder it is configured on. The
931         * event is not changed, so other appenders, other encoders and anything else that
932         * reads the event see the original values.
933         * <p>
934         * Like formatters, post processors must be thread-safe. One instance processes every
935         * event of its encoder, possibly from several threads at once, each with its own
936         * {@link StringBuilder}.
937         * <p>
938         * The {@link StandardPostProcessor}s are registered under their lowercase names when
939         * the {@link LogConfig} is created. Others are added with
940         * {@link #register(ServiceRegistry, String, Provider)}. A name that is not registered
941         * fails when the encoder is provisioned, with an error listing the registered names.
942         */
943        public interface PostProcessor {
944
945                /**
946                 * Rewrites the event's text in place. Only the text from <code>start</code> to
947                 * the end of <code>output</code> belongs to this event; text before
948                 * <code>start</code> must not be changed. <code>output</code> is the encoder's
949                 * buffer, which the encoder sizes and trims, so a post processor that needs
950                 * working space should use <code>output</code> itself, for example by appending
951                 * the rewritten text and deleting the original, rather than a buffer of its own.
952                 * @param event the event that was formatted.
953                 * @param output the output, whose text from <code>start</code> to its end is the
954                 * event's text.
955                 * @param start index where the event's text begins.
956                 */
957                void process(LogEvent event, StringBuilder output, int start);
958
959                /**
960                 * Wraps a formatter so this post processor rewrites everything it writes.
961                 * @param formatter formatter to wrap.
962                 * @return formatter.
963                 */
964                default LogFormatter decorate(LogFormatter formatter) {
965                        return new PostProcessingFormatter(formatter, this);
966                }
967
968                /**
969                 * Registers a post processor under a name so encoders can select it with
970                 * {@value LogEncoder#ENCODER_POST_PROCESSORS_PROPERTY}, usually from a
971                 * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator}. A name
972                 * that is already registered, including the name of a
973                 * {@link StandardPostProcessor}, is not replaced.
974                 * @param registry usually {@link LogConfig#serviceRegistry()}.
975                 * @param name the name used in the property.
976                 * @param provider creates the post processor, given the encoder's name and
977                 * config.
978                 */
979                public static void register(ServiceRegistry registry, String name, Provider provider) {
980                        registry.put(Provider.class, name, provider);
981                }
982
983                /**
984                 * Creates a post processor for an encoder, given the encoder's name and config.
985                 * It is called once each time an encoder that lists its name is built, not for
986                 * each event.
987                 */
988                @FunctionalInterface
989                public interface Provider extends LogProvider<PostProcessor> {
990
991                }
992
993        }
994
995        /**
996         * The built in post processors, selected by their lowercase names.
997         */
998        @CaseChanging
999        public enum StandardPostProcessor implements PostProcessor {
1000
1001                /**
1002                 * Starts every line of the event with its syslog severity as
1003                 * <code>&lt;N&gt;</code> (error 3, warning 4, info 6, debug and trace 7), which
1004                 * systemd's journal reads as the line's priority when standard out or standard
1005                 * err is connected to it. Every line is prefixed, including stack trace lines,
1006                 * because the journal stores each line as its own entry.
1007                 */
1008                JOURNALD {
1009                        @Override
1010                        public void process(LogEvent event, StringBuilder output, int start) {
1011                                PostProcessors.prefixLines(output, start, PostProcessors.journaldPrefix(event.level()));
1012                        }
1013                },
1014                /**
1015                 * Escapes carriage returns and line feeds inside the event's text as backslash
1016                 * <code>r</code> and backslash <code>n</code>, so each event stays on one line
1017                 * and text logged from untrusted input cannot start a forged line. A trailing
1018                 * line separator ending the event is kept.
1019                 */
1020                CRLF {
1021                        @Override
1022                        public void process(LogEvent event, StringBuilder output, int start) {
1023                                PostProcessors.escapeLineBreaks(output, start);
1024                        }
1025                };
1026
1027        }
1028
1029}

1031@SuppressWarnings("ArrayRecordComponent")
1032record CompositeFormatter(LogFormatter[] formatters) implements EventFormatter {
1033
1034        static String[] SPACES = { " ", "  ", "    ", "        ", // 1,2,4,8 spaces
1035                        "                ", // 16 spaces
1036                        "                                " }; // 32 spaces
1037
1038        @Override
1039        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
1040                for (var formatter : formatters) {
1041                        formatter.format(output, event);
1042                }
1043        }
1044
1045        @Override
1046        public String toString() {
1047                return getClass().getSimpleName() + Arrays.toString(formatters);
1048        }
1049
1050        public static List<LogFormatter> flatten(List<? extends LogFormatter> formatters) {
1051                return List.copyOf(_flatten(formatters));
1052        }
1053
1054        private static List<LogFormatter> _flatten(List<? extends LogFormatter> formatters) {
1055                List<LogFormatter> result = new ArrayList<>();
1056                for (var f : formatters) {
1057                        if (f instanceof CompositeFormatter cf) {
1058                                result.addAll(_flatten(cf));
1059                        }
1060                        else {
1061                                result.add(f);
1062                        }
1063                }
1064                return result;
1065        }
1066
1067        private static List<LogFormatter> _flatten(CompositeFormatter formatter) {
1068                var formatters = formatter.formatters;
1069                return _flatten(Arrays.asList(formatters));
1070        }
1071
1072}

1132/**
1133 * Not an enum: error-prone's immutable-enum check flags enums holding mutable state, and
1134 * {@link #cache} is mutable (an {@link java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference}).
1135 * {@link #description} exists solely to give each instance a stable identity for
1136 * {@link #toString()}.
1137 */
1138final class DefaultInstantFormatter implements TimestampFormatter {
1139
1140        static final DefaultInstantFormatter TTLL = new DefaultInstantFormatter("TTLL",
1141                        DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern(TTLL_TIME_FORMAT).withZone(ZoneId.from(ZoneOffset.UTC)));
1142
1143        /*
1144         * appendInstant(3) renders a fixed-width 3-digit millisecond fraction (unlike
1145         * DateTimeFormatter.ISO_DATE_TIME, which renders a variable-width fraction of 0-9
1146         * digits based on the instant's actual sub-millisecond value) - fixed width matches
1147         * Logback/Log4j2's ISO output and is what makes this safe to millis-cache.
1148         */
1149        static final DefaultInstantFormatter ISO = new DefaultInstantFormatter("ISO",
1150                        new DateTimeFormatterBuilder().appendInstant(3).toFormatter());
1151
1152        private final String description;
1153
1154        private final DateTimeFormatter formatter;
1155
1156        private final MillisCache cache = new MillisCache();
1157
1158        private DefaultInstantFormatter(String description, DateTimeFormatter formatter) {
1159                this.description = description;
1160                this.formatter = formatter;
1161        }
1162
1163        @Override
1164        public void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant) {
1165                cache.formatTimestamp(output, instant, formatter);
1166        }
1167
1168        @Override
1169        public String toString() {
1170                return description;
1171        }
1172

1175/**
1176 * Micro seconds over the events last second, for Logback compatibility - meant to be
1177 * composed after a millisecond-precision timestamp (see
1178 * {@link TimestampFormatter#ofISO()}). Stateless, so a singleton enum works cleanly here
1179 * (unlike {@link DefaultInstantFormatter}, nothing here trips error-prone's
1180 * immutable-enum check).
1181 */
1182enum MicrosInstantFormatter implements TimestampFormatter {
1183
1184        INSTANCE;
1185
1186        @Override
1187        @SuppressWarnings("JavaInstantGetSecondsGetNano")
1188        public void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant) {
1189                int nanos = instant.getNano();
1190
1191                int millis_and_micros = nanos / 1000;
1192                int micros = millis_and_micros % 1000;
1193
1194                if (micros >= 100) {
1195                        output.append(micros);
1196                }
1197                else if (micros >= 10) {
1198                        output.append("0").append(micros);
1199                }
1200                else {
1201                        output.append("00").append(micros);
1202                }
1203        }
1204
1205}

1214                this.dateTimeFormatter = dateTimeFormatter;
1215                this.cache = cacheMillisecondPrecision ? new MillisCache() : null;
1216        }

1219        public void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant) {
1220                var c = cache;
1221                if (c == null) {
1222                        dateTimeFormatter.formatTo(instant, output);
1223                        return;
1224                }

1230/**
1231 * Caches a formatted timestamp string keyed by the instant's millisecond value, the same
1232 * trick Logback's {@code CachingDateFormatter} and Log4j2's {@code FixedDateFormat} use -
1233 * reformatting only happens when consecutive events land in different milliseconds. Only
1234 * correct for formatters whose output is fully determined by millisecond precision
1235 * (callers are responsible for that guarantee).
1236 */
1237final class MillisCache {
1238
1239        private record Entry(long millis, String formatted) {
1240        }
1241
1242        private static final Entry EMPTY = new Entry(Long.MIN_VALUE, "");
1243
1244        private final AtomicReference<Entry> ref = new AtomicReference<>(EMPTY);
1245
1246        void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant, DateTimeFormatter formatter) {
1247                long millis = instant.toEpochMilli();
1248                Entry cached = ref.get();
1249                if (cached.millis() == millis) {
1250                        output.append(cached.formatted());
1251                        return;
1252                }
1253                StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(32);
1254                formatter.formatTo(instant, sb);
1255                String formatted = sb.toString();
1256                ref.set(new Entry(millis, formatted));
1257                output.append(formatted);
1258        }
1259
1260}

1273/**
1274 * Prints stack frames trimmed by {@link Builder#maxLines(int) maxLines}/
1275 * {@link Builder#excludes(List) excludes} and optionally appended with packaging data -
1276 * shared as-is between {@link StandardThrowableFormatter} and
1277 * {@link RootCauseFirstThrowableFormatter}, which differ only in traversal order and
1278 * caption choice, never in how an individual throwable's own frames get printed.
1279 */
1280final class ThrowableFramePrinter {
1281
1282        private final int maxLines;
1283
1284        private final List<Pattern> excludes;
1285
1286        private final @Nullable PackagingDataResolver packagingData;
1287
1288        ThrowableFramePrinter(int maxLines, List<Pattern> excludes, @Nullable PackagingDataResolver packagingData) {
1289                this.maxLines = maxLines;
1290                this.excludes = excludes;
1291                this.packagingData = packagingData;
1292        }
1293
1294        /*
1295         * Prints trace's frames, trimmed against enclosingTrace's shared trailing frames (a
1296         * throwable typically shares a stack-trace suffix with whatever holds it as its
1297         * cause, from how the JVM captures traces at throw time) the same way
1298         * Throwable#printStackTrace() does - "... N more" if elision fully accounts for the
1299         * missing frames, nothing if maxLines/excludes already cut the visible output short
1300         * first. Shared verbatim by StandardThrowableFormatter (enclosingTrace = the trace of
1301         * whatever this throwable is the cause of) and RootCauseFirstThrowableFormatter
1302         * (enclosingTrace = the same relationship, just discovered while recursing the other
1303         * direction) - the "which throwable wraps which" relationship this depends on does
1304         * not change with print order.
1305         */
1306        void printFramesAgainstEnclosing(StringBuilder output, StackTraceElement[] trace,
1307                        StackTraceElement[] enclosingTrace, String prefix) {
1308                int m = trace.length - 1;
1309                int n = enclosingTrace.length - 1;
1310                while (m >= 0 && n >= 0 && trace[m].equals(enclosingTrace[n])) {
1311                        m--;
1312                        n--;
1313                }
1314                int framesInCommon = trace.length - 1 - m;
1315                boolean truncated = printFrames(output, trace, m + 1, prefix);
1316                if (!truncated && framesInCommon > 0) {
1317                        output.append(prefix)
1318                                .append("\t... ")
1319                                .append(framesInCommon)
1320                                .append(" more")
1321                                .append(LogFormatter.lineSeparator());
1322                }
1323        }
1324
1325        /*
1326         * Prints frames trace[0..count) filtered by excludes and capped at maxLines. Returns
1327         * true if there were excluded-filtered frames beyond maxLines (i.e. the output was
1328         * cut short because of maxLines rather than ending naturally).
1329         */
1330        boolean printFrames(StringBuilder output, StackTraceElement[] trace, int count, String prefix) {
1331                int printed = 0;
1332                int available = 0;
1333                for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
1334                        var element = trace[i];
1335                        if (isExcluded(element)) {
1336                                continue;
1337                        }
1338                        available++;
1339                        if (printed < maxLines) {
1340                                output.append(prefix).append("\tat ").append(element);
1341                                // Eclipse null analysis is too dumb about final fields.
1342                                var packagingData = this.packagingData;
1343                                if (packagingData != null) {
1344                                        output.append(' ').append(packagingData.resolve(element));
1345                                }
1346                                output.append(LogFormatter.lineSeparator());
1347                                printed++;
1348                        }
1349                }
1350                if (available > maxLines) {
1351                        output.append(prefix)
1352                                .append("\t... ")
1353                                .append(available - maxLines)
1354                                .append(" frames truncated")
1355                                .append(LogFormatter.lineSeparator());
1356                        return true;
1357                }
1358                return false;
1359        }
1360
1361        private boolean isExcluded(StackTraceElement element) {
1362                if (excludes.isEmpty()) {
1363                        return false;
1364                }
1365                String s = element.toString();
1366                for (var p : excludes) {
1367                        Matcher matcher = p.matcher(s);
1368                        if (matcher.find()) {
1369                                return true;
1370                        }
1371                }
1372                return false;
1373        }
1374
1375}
1376
1377/**
1378 * Reimplements {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()}'s algorithm (header line, frames,
1379 * common-frame elision against the enclosing trace, "Caused by:"/"Suppressed:" sections,
1380 * circular reference guard) so that a max line count and frame exclusion patterns can be
1381 * applied while printing.
1382 */
1383final class StandardThrowableFormatter implements ThrowableFormatter {
1384
1385        private static final String CAUSE_CAPTION = "Caused by: ";
1386
1387        private static final String SUPPRESSED_CAPTION = "Suppressed: ";
1388
1389        private final ThrowableFramePrinter framePrinter;
1390
1391        StandardThrowableFormatter(ThrowableFramePrinter framePrinter) {
1392                this.framePrinter = framePrinter;
1393        }
1394
1395        @Override
1396        public void formatThrowable(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable) {
1397                Set<Throwable> dejaVu = Collections.newSetFromMap(new IdentityHashMap<>());
1398                dejaVu.add(throwable);
1399                var trace = throwable.getStackTrace();
1400                output.append(throwable).append(LogFormatter.lineSeparator());
1401                framePrinter.printFrames(output, trace, trace.length, "");
1402                for (var suppressed : throwable.getSuppressed()) {
1403                        printEnclosed(output, suppressed, trace, SUPPRESSED_CAPTION, "\t", dejaVu);
1404                }
1405                var cause = throwable.getCause();
1406                if (cause != null) {
1407                        printEnclosed(output, cause, trace, CAUSE_CAPTION, "", dejaVu);
1408                }
1409        }
1410
1411        private void printEnclosed(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable, StackTraceElement[] enclosingTrace,
1412                        String caption, String prefix, Set<Throwable> dejaVu) {
1413                if (!dejaVu.add(throwable)) {
1414                        output.append(prefix)
1415                                .append("[CIRCULAR REFERENCE: ")
1416                                .append(throwable)
1417                                .append(']')
1418                                .append(LogFormatter.lineSeparator());
1419                        return;
1420                }
1421                var trace = throwable.getStackTrace();
1422                output.append(prefix).append(caption).append(throwable).append(LogFormatter.lineSeparator());
1423                framePrinter.printFramesAgainstEnclosing(output, trace, enclosingTrace, prefix);
1424                for (var suppressed : throwable.getSuppressed()) {
1425                        printEnclosed(output, suppressed, trace, SUPPRESSED_CAPTION, prefix + "\t", dejaVu);
1426                }
1427                var cause = throwable.getCause();
1428                if (cause != null) {
1429                        printEnclosed(output, cause, trace, CAUSE_CAPTION, prefix, dejaVu);
1430                }
1431        }
1432
1433}
1434
1435/**
1436 * Mirrors logback's <code>RootCauseFirstThrowableProxyConverter</code>: same frame
1437 * trimming/common-frame elision as {@link StandardThrowableFormatter}, but the root cause
1438 * prints first and each wrapper prints afterward, captioned "Wrapped by: " instead of
1439 * "Caused by: ". Common-frame elision for a given throwable is still computed against its
1440 * own direct wrapper's frames (the throwable that has it as {@link Throwable#getCause()})
1441 * regardless of print order - that relationship, and therefore the elision counts, do not
1442 * depend on which order things are printed in.
1443 * <p>
1444 * A suppressed exception's own "Suppressed: " caption lands on the first line actually
1445 * printed for it - the root of <em>its</em> own cause chain if it has one, not the
1446 * suppressed exception's own header - matching logback's
1447 * <code>recursiveAppendRootCauseFirst</code> exactly (the caption is threaded down
1448 * through the recursion and only consumed once, at the bottom).
1449 */
1450final class RootCauseFirstThrowableFormatter implements ThrowableFormatter {
1451
1452        private static final String WRAPPED_BY_CAPTION = "Wrapped by: ";
1453
1454        private static final String SUPPRESSED_CAPTION = "Suppressed: ";
1455
1456        private final ThrowableFramePrinter framePrinter;
1457
1458        RootCauseFirstThrowableFormatter(ThrowableFramePrinter framePrinter) {
1459                this.framePrinter = framePrinter;
1460        }
1461
1462        @Override
1463        public void formatThrowable(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable) {
1464                Set<Throwable> dejaVu = Collections.newSetFromMap(new IdentityHashMap<>());
1465                print(output, throwable, null, null, "", dejaVu);
1466        }
1467
1468        private void print(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable, StackTraceElement @Nullable [] enclosingTrace,
1469                        @Nullable String caption, String prefix, Set<Throwable> dejaVu) {
1470                if (!dejaVu.add(throwable)) {
1471                        output.append(prefix);
1472                        if (caption != null) {
1473                                output.append(caption);
1474                        }
1475                        output.append("[CIRCULAR REFERENCE: ").append(throwable).append(']').append(LogFormatter.lineSeparator());
1476                        return;
1477                }
1478                var trace = throwable.getStackTrace();
1479                var cause = throwable.getCause();
1480                if (cause != null) {
1481                        print(output, cause, trace, caption, prefix, dejaVu);
1482                        caption = null; // consumed by the recursive (deeper) call above
1483                }
1484                output.append(prefix);
1485                if (caption != null) {
1486                        output.append(caption);
1487                }
1488                if (cause != null) {
1489                        output.append(WRAPPED_BY_CAPTION);
1490                }
1491                output.append(throwable).append(LogFormatter.lineSeparator());
1492                if (enclosingTrace == null) {
1493                        framePrinter.printFrames(output, trace, trace.length, prefix);
1494                }
1495                else {
1496                        framePrinter.printFramesAgainstEnclosing(output, trace, enclosingTrace, prefix);
1497                }
1498                for (var suppressed : throwable.getSuppressed()) {
1499                        print(output, suppressed, trace, SUPPRESSED_CAPTION, prefix + "\t", dejaVu);
1500                }
1501        }
1502
1503}
1504
1505/**
1506 * Resolves and caches which jar/module/directory a stack frame's class was loaded from
1507 * and its reported version, formatted as <code>[location:version]</code>. Named modules
1508 * (including JDK frames) are resolved for free from the frame itself or the loaded
1509 * class's {@link Module} without touching a {@link java.security.CodeSource}. Classpath
1510 * (unnamed module) frames fall back to the class's {@link java.security.CodeSource} and
1511 * {@link Package#getImplementationVersion()}. Either "location" or "version" is
1512 * <code>na</code> when unknown, and the whole result is <code>[na:na]</code> when the
1513 * frame's class cannot be loaded at all (e.g. dynamically generated classes).
1514 */
1515final class PackagingDataResolver {
1516
1517        private final ConcurrentMap<String, String> cache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
1518
1519        String resolve(StackTraceElement element) {
1520                String className = element.getClassName();
1521                String cached = cache.get(className);
1522                if (cached != null) {
1523                        return cached;
1524                }
1525                String computed = compute(element);
1526                cache.put(className, computed);
1527                return computed;
1528        }
1529
1530        private static String compute(StackTraceElement element) {
1531                String moduleName = element.getModuleName();
1532                if (moduleName != null) {
1533                        return format(moduleName, element.getModuleVersion());
1534                }
1535                Class<?> type = load(element.getClassName());
1536                if (type == null) {
1537                        return "[na:na]";
1538                }
1539                Module module = type.getModule();
1540                if (module.isNamed()) {
1541                        var descriptor = module.getDescriptor();
1542                        String version = descriptor == null ? null : descriptor.rawVersion().orElse(null);
1543                        return format(module.getName(), version);
1544                }
1545                var codeSource = type.getProtectionDomain().getCodeSource();
1546                if (codeSource == null) {
1547                        return "[na:na]";
1548                }
1549                var location = codeSource.getLocation();
1550                if (location == null) {
1551                        return "[na:na]";
1552                }
1553                String path = location.getPath();
1554                if (path == null || path.isEmpty()) {
1555                        path = location.toString();
1556                }
1557                if (path.endsWith("/")) {
1558                        path = path.substring(0, path.length() - 1);
1559                }
1560                int slash = path.lastIndexOf('/');
1561                String name = slash >= 0 && slash < path.length() - 1 ? path.substring(slash + 1) : path;
1562                var pkg = type.getPackage();
1563                String version = pkg == null ? null : pkg.getImplementationVersion();
1564                return format(name, version);
1565        }
1566
1567        private static String format(String location, @Nullable String version) {
1568                return "[" + location + ":" + (version == null || version.isEmpty() ? "na" : version) + "]";
1569        }
1570
1571        private static @Nullable Class<?> load(String className) {
1572                var contextLoader = Thread.currentThread().getContextClassLoader();
1573                if (contextLoader != null) {
1574                        var type = loadOrNull(className, contextLoader);
1575                        if (type != null) {
1576                                return type;
1577                        }
1578                }
1579                return loadOrNull(className, PackagingDataResolver.class.getClassLoader());
1580        }
1581
1582        private static @Nullable Class<?> loadOrNull(String className, @Nullable ClassLoader loader) {
1583                try {
1584                        return Class.forName(className, false, loader);
1585                }
1586                catch (ClassNotFoundException | LinkageError | SecurityException e) {
1587                        return null;
1588                }
1589        }
1590
1591}
1592
1593record SingleKeyValueFormatter(String key, @Nullable String fallback) implements LogFormatter {
1594        @Override
1595        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
1596                var kvs = event.keyValues();
1597                formatKeyValues(output, kvs);
1598        }
1599
1600        void formatKeyValues(StringBuilder output, KeyValues keyValues) {
1601                String v = keyValues.getValueOrNull(key);
1602                if (v == null) {
1603                        v = fallback;
1604                }
1605                PercentCodec.encode(output, key, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1606                if (v != null) {
1607                        output.append('=');
1608                        PercentCodec.encode(output, v, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1609                }
1610        }
1611
1612}
1613
1614/**
1615 * Logback/Log4j2 <code>%X{key}</code> style: just the raw value (or fallback, or empty
1616 * string), no key prefix, no percent encoding. See
1617 * {@link LogFormatter.Builder#keyValue(String, String)}.
1618 */
1619record LogbackSingleKeyValueFormatter(String key, @Nullable String fallback) implements LogFormatter {
1620
1621        @Override
1622        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
1623                var kvs = event.keyValues();
1624                String v = kvs.getValueOrNull(key);
1625                if (v == null) {
1626                        v = fallback;
1627                }
1628                if (v != null) {
1629                        output.append(v);
1630                }
1631        }
1632
1633}
1634
1635/*
1636 * Applies a post processor to the region of the output a formatter wrote for an event.
1637 */
1638record PostProcessingFormatter(LogFormatter formatter,
1639                LogFormatter.PostProcessor postProcessor) implements LogFormatter.EventFormatter {
1640
1641        @Override
1642        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
1643                int start = output.length();
1644                formatter.format(output, event);
1645                if (output.length() > start) {
1646                        postProcessor.process(event, output, start);
1647                }
1648        }
1649
1650}
1651
1652final class PostProcessors {
1653
1654        private PostProcessors() {
1655        }
1656
1657        /*
1658         * Registers the standard post processors under their lowercase names. Called when the
1659         * LogConfig is created, before any configurator can register a name.
1660         */
1661        static void registerStandard(ServiceRegistry registry) {
1662                for (var standard : LogFormatter.StandardPostProcessor.values()) {
1663                        LogFormatter.PostProcessor.register(registry, standard.name().toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT),
1664                                        (n, c) -> standard);
1665                }
1666        }
1667
1668        /*
1669         * Resolves the post processors named by the encoder's postProcessors property, in
1670         * order, and wraps the formatter with them.
1671         */
1672        static LogFormatter decorate(LogFormatter formatter, String encoderName, LogConfig config) {
1673                String key = LogProperties.interpolateKey(LogEncoder.ENCODER_POST_PROCESSORS_PROPERTY,
1674                                java.util.Map.of(LogProperties.NAME, encoderName));
1675                List<String> names = config.properties().forKey(key).ofList().or(List.of()).validateNow(LogEncoder.class);
1676                LogFormatter result = formatter;
1677                for (String name : names) {
1678                        result = resolve(name.strip(), encoderName, config).decorate(result);
1679                }
1680                return result;
1681        }
1682
1683        private static LogFormatter.PostProcessor resolve(String name, String encoderName, LogConfig config) {
1684                var provider = config.serviceRegistry().findOrNull(LogFormatter.PostProcessor.Provider.class, name);
1685                if (provider != null) {
1686                        return provider.provide(encoderName, config);
1687                }
1688                var available = new java.util.TreeSet<String>();
1689                config.serviceRegistry().forEach(LogFormatter.PostProcessor.Provider.class, (n, p) -> available.add(n));
1690                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown post processor '" + name + "' for encoder '" + encoderName
1691                                + "'. Available post processors: " + String.join(", ", available));
1692        }
1693
1694        /*
1695         * Puts the prefix at the start of the region and after each line break that is
1696         * followed by more text. Inserting per line shifts the rest of the region each time,
1697         * which is quadratic for a long stack trace, so the prefixed copy is appended after
1698         * the region in one pass and the original is then deleted.
1699         */
1700        static void prefixLines(StringBuilder output, int start, String prefix) {
1701                int end = output.length();
1702                int lineStart = start;
1703                output.append(prefix);
1704                for (int i = start; i < end - 1; i++) {
1705                        if (output.charAt(i) == '\n') {
1706                                output.append(output, lineStart, i + 1).append(prefix);
1707                                lineStart = i + 1;
1708                        }
1709                }
1710                output.append(output, lineStart, end);
1711                output.delete(start, end);
1712        }
1713
1714        /*
1715         * Escapes CR and LF in the region except a single trailing line separator.
1716         */
1717        static void escapeLineBreaks(StringBuilder output, int start) {
1718                int end = output.length();
1719                if (end > start && output.charAt(end - 1) == '\n') {
1720                        end--;
1721                        if (end > start && output.charAt(end - 1) == '\r') {
1722                                end--;
1723                        }
1724                }
1725                for (int i = end - 1; i >= start; i--) {
1726                        char c = output.charAt(i);
1727                        if (c == '\n') {
1728                                output.replace(i, i + 1, "\\n");
1729                        }
1730                        else if (c == '\r') {
1731                                output.replace(i, i + 1, "\\r");
1732                        }
1733                }
1734        }
1735
1736        /*
1737         * Syslog severities. OFF is not a real event level; it maps to info rather than 0
1738         * (emergency), which journald broadcasts to every logged in terminal.
1739         */
1740        static String journaldPrefix(Level level) {
1741                return switch (level) {
1742                        case ERROR -> "<3>";
1743                        case WARNING -> "<4>";
1744                        case INFO, OFF -> "<6>";
1745                        case DEBUG, TRACE, ALL -> "<7>";
1746                };
1747        }
1748
1749}
